If $\mathrm{num} \cdot \mathrm{tden} = \mathrm{tnum} \cdot \mathrm{den}$ and $\mathrm{tnum}/\mathrm{tden}$ is palindromic, then so is $\mathrm{num}/\mathrm{den}$. Pointwise transfer fails at the poles of $\mathrm{tden}$, so the proof establishes the polynomial identity $\widetilde{\mathrm{num}} \cdot \mathrm{den} = \mathrm{num} \cdot \widetilde{\mathrm{den}}$ (tilde = coefficient reversal) on a cofinite set and extends it everywhere by the identity theorem.
nodes.lean:
theorem isPalindromic_of_agree
    (num den tnum tden : Polynomial ℚ)
    (hden : den ≠ 0) (htden : tden ≠ 0)
    (hagree : num * tden = tnum * den)
    (htpalin : IsPalindromic tnum tden) :
    IsPalindromic num den
nodes.note: The transfer itself is proved; its input — palindromy at the tame primes — is the hypothesis still open on the real instance, which keeps the functional-equation clause of the capstone conditional.

nodes.title: What one node of the Montes tree carries
nodes.math: A shape packages the data of one node of the Okutsu–Montes tree at order $r$: a finite residue field $F_r$ with an algebra structure over the base residue field $\mathbb{F}$, so the residue degree is the true extension degree $[F_r : \mathbb{F}]$ rather than a free integer; the order-$r$ residual polynomial over $F_r$, its recorded degree tied to its actual degree; the order-$r$ lattice Newton polygon; and the cluster size that serves as the well-founded descent measure.
nodes.lean:
structure OMShape where
  size : ℕ
  order : ℕ
  Fr : Type
  [instField : Field Fr]
  [instFinite : Finite Fr]
  baseField : Type
  [instBaseField : Field baseField]
  [instBaseFinite : Finite baseField]
  [instAlg : Algebra baseField Fr]
  residueDeg : ℕ
  hResidueDeg : residueDeg = Module.finrank baseField Fr
  polygon : L4.LatticePolygon
  residual : Polynomial Fr
  residualDeg : ℕ
  hResidualDeg : residualDeg = residual.natDegree
nodes.note: The proof-carrying fields make degenerate instantiations impossible: with them $|F_r| = q^{[F_r : \mathbb{F}]}$ is a lemma rather than an assumption, and every downstream count comes from a polynomial over a field extension.

nodes.title: Three structural facts about the Montes tree, cited from Guardia–Montes–Nart
nodes.math: Three facts about the Okutsu–Montes tree are cited from Guardia–Montes–Nart (Trans. AMS 364, 2012) and declared as axioms: every shape carries a finite list of order-$r$ cells, one per Newton-polygon face and residual stratum; a descent operation produces the child shapes; and every child of every cell has strictly smaller cluster size — the well-foundedness that drives the induction. None of the three asserts a volume, a rationality, or any $p$-independence; those are always derived.
nodes.lean:
axiom omCells : (T : OMShape) → List (OMCell T)

axiom descend : OMShape → List OMShape

axiom descend_size_lt :
    ∀ (T : OMShape), ∀ c ∈ omCells T, ∀ ch ∈ c.children, ch.node.size < T.size
nodes.note: Only the measure route uses these axioms; the count-native capstones avoid them. One point remains open: whether the cell strata jointly reconstruct the full residual.

nodes.title: The cited Denef–Igusa recursion for the p-adic cluster measure
nodes.math: For a prime $p$ and integer $q > 1$: one fixed symbol denotes the conditional $p$-adic Haar measure of each shape’s cluster — mathlib has no $p$-adic Haar measure, so the object itself is declared as an axiom — and the load-bearing cited axiom asserts Igusa and Denef’s cell decomposition for it: the cluster measure equals $\big(\sum_{\text{cells}} (\text{residual point count}) \cdot (\text{Newton-box volume}) \cdot \prod_{\text{children}} (\text{child measure})\big) \big/ (1 - q^{-w})$, with $w$ the self-loop exponent and $1 - q^{-w}$ the geometric self-loop pivot. A structural factorization of a measure, never a rationality claim (Igusa, *Local Zeta Functions* §7.4; Denef, *Invent. Math.* 77 (1984)).
nodes.lean:
axiom clusterMeasure : OMShape → ℕ → ℚ

axiom AX_cellRecursion (T : OMShape) (q : ℕ) (hq : 1 < q) :
    clusterMeasure T q
      = ((omCells T).map (fun c =>
            residualCountFn T c.residualDeg q
            * L4.bb1Value c.polygon q
            * (c.children.map (fun ch => clusterMeasure ch.node q)).prod)).sum
        / omPivot T q
nodes.note: The axiom names one fixed object rather than a freely quantified pivot, which would be inconsistent, and comes with an explicit model witnessing its satisfiability.

nodes.title: An explicit model witnesses that the cell-recursion axiom is satisfiable
nodes.math: A function constructed by well-founded recursion on cluster size — descending along the strict-descent axiom — satisfies the identity that the cell-recursion axiom asserts. The axiom is therefore satisfiable, hence relatively consistent; by contrast, quantifying the pivot freely over all values would force $1 = 1/2$, so only the fixed-object form is consistent.
nodes.lean:
theorem clusterMeasureModel_rec (T : OMShape) (q : ℕ) (hq : 1 < q) :
    clusterMeasureModel T q
      = ((omCells T).map (fun c =>
            residualCountFn T c.residualDeg q
            * L4.bb1Value c.polygon q
            * (c.children.map (fun ch => clusterMeasureModel ch.node q)).prod)).sum
        / omPivot T q
nodes.note: This model certifies that the cell-recursion axiom is satisfiable.

nodes.title: Measure route: every cluster measure is one rational function of q
nodes.math: For a prime $p$, residue size $q > 1$, and self-loop exponent $w$: the fixed conditional $p$-adic cluster measure of every Okutsu–Montes shape is a uniform rational function of $q$. The cited cell recursion discharges the recursion hypothesis of the abstract engine; every other input is proved — strict descent from the cited tree structure, coefficient rationality from the finite-field residual count times the Newton-box volume, and pole-freeness of the self-loop pivot $1 - q^{-w}$. No axiom mentions rationality; it emerges only through the induction.
nodes.lean:
theorem clusterMeasure_isRational_of_AX :
    ∀ T : OMShape, IsRationalFn (clusterMeasure T)
nodes.gate: clusterMeasure, the opaque cited p-adic Haar cluster-measure interface object; AX_cellRecursion, the cited Denef–Igusa cell-decomposition identity for it; omCells / descend_size_lt, the cited GMN finite cell partition and strict size descent
nodes.note: A complete second route to rationality, conditional on the cited measure axioms and independent of the count-native chain, whose capstones avoid every axiom named in this gate.

nodes.title: The count-native cluster recursion, built from proved counts alone
nodes.math: For a cluster shape $T$ and integer $q \ge 2$, a cluster count defined by well-founded recursion on tree size: $\mathrm{count}(T,q) = \big(\sum_{\text{cells } c} (q^{\delta})^{d_S-1} \cdot \mathrm{box}(c,q) \cdot \prod_{\text{children}} \mathrm{count}(\cdot,q)\big) \big/ \big(1 - q^{-w(s)}\big)$, where $\delta$ is the cell’s residue degree, $(q^{\delta})^{d_S-1}$ is the proved count of non-squarefree residuals of degree $d_S$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^{\delta}}$, $\mathrm{box}(c,q)$ is the proved Newton-box volume, and $w(s) = s(s+1)/2 - 1$ is the self-loop exponent at cluster size $s$. No opaque measure object appears anywhere.
nodes.lean:
noncomputable def clusterCount
    (cells : ClusterShape → List CountCell) (treeSize : ClusterShape → ℕ)
    (hdesc : ∀ (T : ClusterShape), ∀ c ∈ cells T, ∀ ch ∈ c.children, treeSize ch < treeSize T)
    (T : ClusterShape) (q : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  ((cells T).attach.map (fun c =>
      countCellCoeff c.1 q
        * (c.1.children.attach.map (fun ch => clusterCount cells treeSize hdesc ch.1 q)).prod)).sum
    / countPivot (treeSize T) q
nodes.note: Because every ingredient is a proved counting block, the density capstones built on it need no measure axioms at all.

nodes.title: Exactly Q^(d−1) residual configurations trigger refinement
nodes.math: Over a finite field $F$ with $Q = |F|$, the monic polynomials of degree $d_S \ge 2$ that are not squarefree — precisely the residuals that force a further refinement step — number exactly $Q^{d_S - 1}$: the monic total $Q^{d_S}$ minus the squarefree count $Q^{d_S} - Q^{d_S - 1}$.
nodes.note: The $q$-varying wild factor inside every cell coefficient; a constant here would leave the wild mechanism unexercised.

nodes.title: Density means the limit of decided counts
nodes.math: A counting model at residue size $q \ge 2$ and degree $n$ records, for each factorization type $\sigma$ and precision $N$, how many coefficient boxes mod $p^N$ ($p$ the underlying prime) have their type already determined by their digits (decided) and how many do not (undecided), subject to: decided plus undecided partition the full box of $q^{nN}$; the normalized decided counts are monotone in $N$ and converge; and mass newly decided after level $N$ is drawn from the level-$N$ undecided pool. The density of $\sigma$ is defined as that decided limit — never the trivial box count, which is identically $1$.
nodes.lean:
structure CountingModel (q n : ℕ) where
  hq : 2 ≤ q
  decidedCount : FactorizationType → ℕ → ℚ
  undecidedCount : ℕ → ℚ
  decidedCount_nonneg : ∀ σ N, 0 ≤ decidedCount σ N
  undecidedCount_nonneg : ∀ N, 0 ≤ undecidedCount N
  typeMenu : Finset FactorizationType
  typeMenu_degree : ∀ σ ∈ typeMenu, σ.degree = n
  decidedCount_off_menu : ∀ σ N, σ ∉ typeMenu → decidedCount σ N = 0
  box_partition : ∀ N, (∑ σ ∈ typeMenu, decidedCount σ N) + undecidedCount N = (q : ℚ) ^ (n * N)
  decided_mono : ∀ σ, Monotone (fun N => decidedCount σ N / (q : ℚ) ^ (n * N))
  densityVal : FactorizationType → ℚ
  decided_tendsto : ∀ σ, Filter.Tendsto (fun N => decidedCount σ N / (q : ℚ) ^ (n * N))
    Filter.atTop (nhds (densityVal σ))
  upper_tail : ∀ (σ : FactorizationType) (N K : ℕ), N ≤ K →
    decidedCount σ K / (q : ℚ) ^ (n * K)
      ≤ decidedCount σ N / (q : ℚ) ^ (n * N) + undecidedCount N / (q : ℚ) ^ (n * N)
nodes.note: This fixes the semantics of the whole counting route — a density is a limit of decided counts — and realizing the structure with $p$-adic digit counts is what the real instances in the OM corpus do.

nodes.title: Vanishing undecided mass squeezes out the density
nodes.math: In a counting model at residue size $q \ge 2$ and degree $n$, for a factorization type $\sigma$ both brackets hold at every level $N$: $\mathrm{decided}(\sigma,N) \le \rho(\sigma) \le \mathrm{decided}(\sigma,N) + \mathrm{undecided}(N)$, where $\rho(\sigma)$ is the decided limit and all quantities are normalized by $q^{nN}$. If the undecided mass tends to $0$, the upper bracket also converges to $\rho(\sigma)$: the density is the unique value caught between brackets of vanishing width.
nodes.lean:
theorem countingDensity_is_squeezed_limit {q n : ℕ} (M : CountingModel q n)
    (hU : UndecidedVanishes M) (σ : FactorizationType) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun N => M.decidedMeasure σ N + M.undecided N) Filter.atTop
      (nhds (M.countingDensity σ))
nodes.note: The vanishing-undecided hypothesis is the termination content — the classifier must eventually decide almost every polynomial; it is proved for the full degree-2 model and open in general.

nodes.title: The box count is the total over all types, never a density
nodes.math: For a prime $p$ and degree $n$, at every precision $N$ the full box measure, identically $1$, equals the sum over all factorization types $\sigma$ of the decided measures plus the undecided remainder. The trivial count of all monic degree-$n$ polynomials mod $p^N$ is therefore the partition total across every type — not the density of any single type $\sigma$.
nodes.lean:
theorem box_is_total_not_density (N : ℕ) :
    M.boxMeasure N = (∑ σ ∈ M.typeMenu, M.decidedMeasure σ N) + M.undecided N
nodes.note: This theorem forecloses the classic failure mode of a density result that secretly computes the trivial total $1$.

nodes.title: The self-loop collapse is a nested recursion over set partitions
nodes.math: For an integer $q \ge 2$ and the completely-split cluster volumes $I_m$ ($m \ge 0$, with $I_0 = I_1 = 1$): for $s \ge 3$ the size-$s$ volume $I_s$ is not a single geometric series; the correct equation is $I_s \cdot (1 - q^{-w(s)}) = \sum_P q^{\underline{r}} \prod_{B \in P} q^{-(|B| + \binom{|B|}{2})} I_{|B|}$, summed over set partitions $P$ of $\{1,\dots,s\}$ into $r \ge 2$ blocks, where $q^{\underline{r}} = q(q-1)\cdots(q-r+1)$ counts assignments of distinct residues to the blocks, $w(s) = s(s+1)/2 - 1$ is the self-loop exponent. Every block is strictly smaller than $s$, so the recursion is well-founded.
nodes.lean:
def SatisfiesNested (I : ℕ → ℕ → ℚ) : Prop :=
  (∀ q, I 0 q = 1) ∧ (∀ q, I 1 q = 1) ∧
    ∀ (s q : ℕ), 2 ≤ s → 2 ≤ q →
      I s q * (1 - ((q : ℚ) ^ L5fix.selfLoopExponent s)⁻¹) = nestedRHS I s q
nodes.note: A predicate that a constructed solution must satisfy, not an axiom asserting a conclusion; the naive single-geometric-series collapse is false for $s \ge 3$, and this is the corrected equation.

nodes.title: The nested recursion reproduces the known closed forms of I₂ and I₃
nodes.math: Any $I$ satisfying the nested recursion has $I_3 = q^3(q^2 - q + 1) \big/ \big((q+1)(q^4+q^3+q^2+q+1)\big)$ for all $q \ge 2$, and a companion theorem gives $I_2 = q/(q+1)$: the set partitions of three elements into at least two blocks — four of them — are listed outright, their weights computed, and the pole-free self-loop pivot inverted.

nodes.title: The carry cocycle: what fails to multiply, exactly
nodes.math: Fix a tower of $n{+}1$ Newton-polygon reads $(e_j, h_j, \psi_j)$, $j = 0,\dots,n$, with $\gcd(e_j,h_j)=1$, over a residue field — the model of one depth-$(n{+}1)$ branch of the classifier, with each stage lifted to the next by the canonical $\varepsilon$-corrected lift (the 'standard-lift harness tower class'). Each eligible index $\gamma$ carries an anchor monomial $\varphi_\gamma$ with a leading value $\mathrm{val}(\varphi_\gamma)$. The carry cocycle is $c_{n+1}(\gamma,\gamma') = \mathrm{val}(\varphi_\gamma\varphi_{\gamma'})/\mathrm{val}(\varphi_{\gamma+\gamma'})$ — the exact correction by which anchor values fail to be multiplicative in the index. It satisfies the 2-cocycle (associativity) identity and descends to $\mathbb{Z}/E_{n+1}$, $E_{n+1} = e_0\cdots e_n$; the deeper transport laws of the tower factor through it. The class is a model: a pinned calculus, consumed as a definition (code of record, not prose), faithful to the classifier's shape — reads, growing residue fields, digit carries.
nodes.note: This is the object the whole stage is about. Wildness lives here: at a tame prime the tower has one read and the cocycle is trivial; at a wild prime the tower is deep and the cocycle records how digit overflow at one level feeds every level below it.

nodes.title: The ε-chain gauge: one normalization, one honest carry
nodes.math: The mechanism behind the laws is simpler than the laws. Modulo the single top carry, the entire cocycle is an explicit coboundary: $c_{n+1} = \bar z^{\,\delta}\cdot\partial F_n$ with $F_n(\gamma) = \prod_{j=1}^n \varepsilon_j(\beta_j(\gamma))$ — one explicitly computable unit per level, the $\varepsilon$-chain. Normalize every anchor by its $\varepsilon$-chain and multiplication becomes exact except for one carry at the top of the tower, inflated from $\mathbb{Z}/e_n$; all the recursion's constants ($D_j$, the composed shifts) are the exponent bookkeeping of $\partial F_n$. The only gauge-independent content is the top carry and one invariant class, $\mathrm{class}(c_{n+1}) = \big[\prod_j z_{j+1}^{(e_0\cdots e_{j-1})\ell_j}\big]$. The all-orders strategy of record follows: per level, prove L6-$(n)$ (anchor value $=$ $\varepsilon$-chain — routine) and W-MULT-$(n)$ (products develop with exactly the top carry — the one hard step); the closed form, integrality, cocycle identity, and the recursion are then derived corollaries, never guessed constant-by-constant again.
nodes.note: At depths 2 and 3 this reading is part of the accepted proofs. As an all-orders mechanism it was the strategy of record — converged on by five decorrelated numeric methods with zero splits (convergence judgment dated 2026-08-03) — and the accepted all-orders theorem (previous nodes) is proved on exactly this plan; its per-level presentation $K[u]/(u^{E} - \sigma)$ visibly echoes the formalized carry algebra $F[u]/(u^e - \bar z)$ of the previous stage — that identification is conjecture-grade and is part of the open weld below.

nodes.title: The machine census: an acceptance question closed by program
nodes.math: The all-orders note's acceptance stalled not on mathematics but on a completeness question: does the note anywhere claim a dependency it does not have, and is every dependency-flavored sentence of the pinned text enumerated and adjudicated? Hand censuses kept diverging — round five's closed sentence mis-counted the pinned text in both directions. Round six replaced the reader with a program: eight widened lexical patterns run over the pinned note produced 194 raw hits on 147 lines, every hit mapped to an adjudicated class (88 at table-row sites, 21 in seven content-true site families, 53 verification apparatus, 8 quoted external record, 18 non-genre, 6 positive displays), zero unadjudicated. In round seven the second verifier wrote its own scanner from the pattern specification alone — independent code, fresh context — and reproduced the census exactly: 194 of 194 hits, 147 of 147 lines, per-pattern identical, empty symmetric difference. The substantive result, confirmed four times independently and last by machine: zero false dependency claims exist anywhere in the note.
nodes.note: A verification-methodology first for this project: an acceptance-blocking question converted from a reader claim into a machine fact, then reproduced by a second, independently written scanner. Enumeration completeness is exactly the kind of bookkeeping that hand passes get wrong in both directions; the machine census is now the enumeration of record, superseding all hand censuses.

nodes.title: The semantic weld: from the model class to the actual classifier — open
nodes.math: Every accepted law in this stage lives on the standard-lift harness tower class — a pinned model calculus with the classifier's shape. The weld is the missing theorem identifying harness towers, their anchors, and their carry data with the actual Okutsu–Montes types of the formalized classifier, so that the accepted laws transport to the Lean OM tree and ultimately to the density campaign's transition expressions. Its Lean-facing counterpart is the standing order-$\ge 2$ classifier-faithfulness obligation of the formal development. The suspected dictionary — the gauge-invariant class presented as $K[u]/(u^{E}-\sigma)$ matching the formalized carry algebra $F[u]/(u^e - \bar z)$ — is recorded at conjecture grade.

nodes.title: The read functional corrected at source (the FGMN re-derivation) — accepted
nodes.math: A standing question about the engine's read functional was answered at the source. Two compiled obstruction walls (a parity wall and a landing wall) had blocked the glue step of the paper-derived read functional inside the formalization. A from-source re-derivation at transcription scale — re-deriving the functional clause by clause from the cited print rather than from the project's own earlier transcription — delivered the verdict: the glue step does fire at the source; both walls were transcription artifacts of one doubly-scaled clause. The repair is three tokens (a weight field read one stage too late, at three sites of the definitions layer), applied under a separately gated unit with its own post-application hostile pass; the fixed points of the diff — the sites whose semantics the repair must not change — are part of the accepted record.
nodes.note: Accepted in the first days of August 2026 after a fourteen-pass, ten-revision adversarial arc with three independently executed computational legs (passes 3, 9, and 12) and a model-diverse double-clean finish. This closed, end-to-end, the campaign's longest-running repair account.
nodes.gate: Not machine-checked as a whole: the acceptance covers the two-scale diagnosis, the source-fires verdict, the exact three-token diff, and the pinned battery record; the applied diff itself compiles green in the Lean corpus.

nodes.title: The last banked unproved statement, proved outright — the corpus at zero banked
nodes.math: Since July 2026 the Lean corpus carried exactly one banked unproved statement: a Newton-polygon hull-stability bound in the classifier, off the capstone path. The statement: for finite point sets $S, S'$, if every genuine vertex of $S'$ is a point of $S$, every point of $S$ lies weakly above the $S'$-hull, and every $S$-abscissa occurs among the $S'$-abscissas, then the genuine vertex lists coincide. (The two-hypothesis version is false — the development keeps a machine-checked counterexample; the third hypothesis is the repair, available for free at the sole use site.) It is now proved outright, with the statement byte-unchanged, in a dedicated 1,700-line module; the falsifier battery ran clean before the proof (8,000 randomized cases), the full build is green, and the axiom-census printout confirms every capstone footprint unchanged. The corpus carries zero banked statements.
nodes.note: This is the one item in this stage that IS machine-checked: Lean-core footprint, statement fence respected (only ':= by sorry' became a term-mode application of the new core theorem).

    (habove : ∀ P ∈ S, NewtonPolygon.npHeight S' hS' (P.1 : ℚ) ≤ (P.2 : ℚ))
    (habs : ∀ P ∈ S, ∃ Q ∈ S', Q.1 = P.1) :
    NewtonPolygon.npVertices S hS = NewtonPolygon.npVertices S' hS' :=
  NewtonPolygon.npVertices_stable_of_hull_preserved_core S S' hS hS' hpres habove habs
